newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-Charges push Dutch Philips into red for 1996.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Charges push Dutch Philips into red for 1996.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV on Thursday reported a 1996 net loss of 590 million guilders ($312.8 million) after booking net extraordinary charges of over 1.3 billion guilders in the year.
The company reported net profit from normal operations of 723 million guilders and the dividend was held unchanged at 1.60 guilders per common share.
"The year 1996 was a severe disappointment, due to a much lower level of sales growth and costs which grew at a faster rate than sales," Philips said in a statement.
However, the company anticipated its current businesses would continue to grow in 1997.
"We are committed to a return to profitability and to the achievement of a positive cash flow of over one billion guilders.
Chairman Cor Boonstra acknowledged the effect of the extraordinaries and added Philips had not responded quickly enough to market conditions.

"Part of this decline was caused by gearing up our organisation for growth which did not materialise. We were simply not quick enough in reacting to the market," he said in his first annual statement since becoming chairman in October.
"We do not blame the markets, nor our competitors, but rather take full responsibility for our lack of speed," he said.

Charges taken during the year included an 800 million charge to restructure the Sound and Vision unit as well as one billion guilders -- of which 600 million related to loss making German unit Grundig.
Philips is now focusing on existing core businesses rather than moving into new areas.
"At this stage we are focusing on building our 100 existing businesses, rather than acquiring businesses in new areas or strategically reshaping the portfolio," Boonstra said.
Boonstra reiterated his policy of weeding out the company's underperformers and loss makers.
"While this process is not yet complete, it is on schedule, and we are rapidly disposing of actvities that absorb profits, cash and management time."
Philips made a fourth quarter net loss from normal operations of 81 million guilders versus a profit of 1.02 billion guilders in the fourth quarter of 1995.
Analysts had expected Philips to report fourth quarter net profit from normal operations of 387-750 million guilders, with consensus around 526 million.
Shares in Philips initially hovered around Wednesday's closing level of 78.10 guilders after the results came out but by midday they were off 0.90 guilders at 77.20.
